summary: Study ALL open ZX Spectrum emulators source for instant TAP/TZX loading techniques (ROM traps, flashload, turbo-block inject, loader acceleration) -> catalog every technique + a plan to maximise BulbuLator instant-load hit-rate

result.techniqueCatalog:
Every DISTINCT instant/fast-load technique found across the ~22 studies, with users and mechanism:

1) STANDARD-ROM PC TRAP + WHOLE-BLOCK BYTE-INJECT ("flashload"). Users: Fuse/libspectrum, ZEsarUX, UnrealSpeccy/USP, CLK, RustZX, JSSpeccy3, JSpeccy/ZXBaremulator, esxDOS/DivMMC, MiSTer smart_tape, SkoolKit loadtracer, BulbuLator (already). Mechanism: detect the Z80 executing the built-in ROM LD-BYTES loop, skip all edge decoding, copy the block straight into RAM at IX for DE bytes, forge the exact post-loader register/flag state, and resume at the ROM RET. This is THE universal instant path and is deterministic, not heuristic.

2) ROM-IDENTITY / PAGE GATE (trap_check_rom). Users: Fuse (memory_pages.c), ZEsarUX, CLK (classic_rom_offset), RustZX, JSSpeccy3 (page 9/10), MiSTer (rom_en), sizif512 divmmc (basic48_paged). Mechanism: only fire the trap when the genuine 48K-BASIC ROM is the ROM currently paged at 0x0000 (48K=any; 128/+2=ROM1; +2A/+3=ROM3 & not all-RAM; Pentagon=ROM1 & !beta) AND no DivMMC/ESXDOS/+D/DISCiPLE/Opus/TR-DOS shadow ROM is active. A pure O(1) register compare, no checksum.

3) BLOCK-STRUCTURE ELIGIBILITY GATE. Users: Fuse, RustZX, JSSpeccy3. Mechanism: only inject if block type == ROM/standard, tape state == PILOT, and block data length == DE+2 (flag+payload+checksum matches what the loader asked). Otherwise fall to pulse. This is what routes standard-vs-turbo-vs-partial per block, again with zero timing heuristic.

4) SAVE TRAP (mirror). Users: Fuse (EX AF,AF' @0x04D0), ZEsarUX, JSpeccy (0x04D0), DivMMC (0x04C6). Not needed for load but confirms the symmetric hook and the $053F return convention.

5) OPCODE-SIGNATURE LOADER ACCELERATOR (acceleration_detector / do_acceleration). Users: Fuse loader.c, ZEsarUX (ported verbatim). Mechanism: on every IN from port 0xFE, run a byte-walking FSM over the code at PC-6 to fingerprint the loader's edge-sampling loop; recognized families (~9-11): generic ROM/INC-B, Speedlock (XOR C), Alkatraz + "variant" Alkatraz, Bleepload (NOP), Microsphere (AND A), Paul Owens (RET Z), Digital Integration (DEC B), Search/Gremlin (AND 0x40), Dinaload (LD A,0xFF), Space Crusade. On match do_acceleration() pokes B=0xFE/0x00 + C bit5=mic level + carry, POPs the loop's return address into PC, and jumps to the next edge — collapsing the busy-wait. NOTE: this deletes HOST cycles; it is a software-emulator trick and is NOT directly portable to a free-running fabric Z80 (see technique 6 for the hardware equivalent).

6) FABRIC M1-SNOOP + DATA-BUS OPCODE-STUB INJECTION (the real-Z80 turbo instant path). User: MiSTer ZX-Spectrum smart_tape (rtl/tape.sv) — the closest analog to BulbuLator. Mechanism: a real Z80 runs in fabric; hardware snoops M1+addr+rom_en, arms at fetch of 0x0562, then DRIVES the CPU data bus with substitute opcodes: inject 0x00 in [0x56C,0x58F) to collapse pilot/sync wait, and inject a stub {JR $-2 (spin) ; LD L,#nn} in [0x5CA,0x5D8) with a byte_wait/byte_ready handshake so the operand of LD L,n is patched with the next real data byte from a FIFO. The genuine ROM keeps doing all flag/parity/IX/DE bookkeeping; only its slow edge loop is replaced. Header vs data discriminated by snooping T80 regs DE==0x0011 && A==0. Self-disarms when PC leaves [0x53F,0x605) or ROM unpaged.

7) WHOLE-CORE CLOCK WARP DURING LOAD. Users: MiSTer (Z80 clocked to 56MHz while tape_active), ZEsarUX (top_speed_timer, deliberately used INSTEAD of register-poking — they left do_acceleration commented out), Fuse (fastload: throttle-off + mute sound), RustZX (--speed max), USP (FullSpeed while step handler set). Mechanism: run the entire machine unthrottled so even non-injectable turbo/pulse loaders finish fast. Orthogonal to traps; edge-accurate. This is BulbuLator's existing FAST/warp, capped ~4x by contention on real silicon.

8) OFFLINE FULL-CPU SIMULATION → SNAPSHOT INJECT (the >99% coverage lever). User: SkoolKit tap2sna --sim-load / loadtracer.py (Python + C build). Mechanism: boot a Z80 SIMULATOR, auto-type LOAD"", run the ACTUAL loader (any loader) over the tape reduced to pulse edges, fast-forward the loader's own sampling/delay loop via a table of ~43 named commercial-loader accelerators (activision, alkatraz-05/09/0a/0b, codemasters, crl, cybexlab, digital-integration, dinaload, gremlin2, microprose, mirrorsoft, operasoft, realtime, silverbird, speedlock, us-gold, ...) plus generic accelerate-dec-a and contended-in for in-RAM 0xFE samplers; when loading finishes (PC lands in RAM, or ~1s after tape end, or timeout), dump RAM+registers to a snapshot. Author reports ~3 failures across 6800+ files (only contended-memory-timing-critical loaders resist). Maps 1:1 to BulbuLator's ARM Z80 interpreter (task #21) feeding a PCAP/state-load into the fabric Z80.

9) DIVMMC/ESXDOS HARDWARE AUTOMAP + Z80 FIRMWARE SERVE. Users: real DivMMC/DivIDE, ESXDOS, UnoDOS3 (GPL source), Spectrum Next, ZX-Uno; already present in BulbuLator fabric (cores/zx-mister/rtl/divmmc.v). Mechanism: hardware pages an 8K firmware ROM over 0x0000-0x1FFF on M1 fetch of {0x0000,0x0008,0x0038,0x0066,0x04C6,0x0562,0x3Dxx}, unmaps at 0x1FF8-0x1FFF. The firmware's LD-BYTES handler at 0x0562 f_reads the next .TAP block off SD, pokes it to IX/DE, sets carry, and RETs to $053F. Standard-loader TAP only; no audio path so it cannot even pulse-fallback.

10) PHANTOM-TYPIST / AUTO-LOAD. Users: Fuse, CLK (holds ENTER 5s), JSSpeccy3 (SZX loader snapshots), ZEsarUX (initial_tap_sequence), BulbuLator (0xA8/ENTER inject). Mechanism: auto-issue LOAD""/128-menu ENTER, deactivate when the trap first fires. Cosmetic but needed for hands-off loading.

11) TEMPO / READ-RATE AUTO PLAY-STOP HEURISTIC (loader_detect_loader). Users: Fuse loader.c, ZEsarUX, BulbuLator (SMP_CNT/ferate — currently used as the DECISION maker, which is the mistake). Mechanism: watch tstates between port-0xFE reads + delta of B: fast (<=500T) & B±1 for 10 reads → auto-PLAY; slow (>1000T) or bad B for 2 reads → auto-STOP. CRITICAL FINDING: in Fuse/ZEsarUX this only drives auto play/stop convenience; correctness comes from techniques 1+5, never from tempo.

12) PULSE/EDGE REPLAY GENERATOR (universal fallback). Users: everyone (MAME uses ONLY this — 0% instant by design; libspectrum turbo_edge/rom_edge; MiSTer module tape + tzxplayer.vhd; Speccy2010 FIFO; BulbuLator PULSE path). Mechanism: render each block to T-state edges (std timings 2168 pilot / 667+735 sync / 855 bit0 / 1710 bit1, 8063 header / 3223 data pilots) and feed EAR. Correct for any loader, never instant.
result.standardTrapConsensus:
STRONG CONSENSUS across Fuse, ZEsarUX, UnrealSpeccy/USP, CLK, RustZX, JSSpeccy3, JSpeccy, esxDOS/DivMMC and SkoolKit. All trap the same 48K ROM LD-BYTES routine; they differ only by a few bytes in exactly WHERE inside it, all equivalent.

ADDRESSES (48K ROM):
- 0x0556 = LD-BYTES entry (INC D / EX AF,AF' at 0x0557 stashes flag+carry into A'/F' / DI / LD A,0x0F / OUT (0xFE),A / LD HL,0x053F / PUSH HL at 0x0561). SkoolKit traps here; DivMMC automaps here-adjacent.
- 0x0562 = first IN A,(0xFE), immediately after PUSH of the 0x053F return. DivMMC/DivIDE/ESXDOS automap trigger; MiSTer smart_tape arms here; BulbuLator already gates here.
- 0x056B = RET NZ (LD-BREAK) at top of the sampling loop. UnrealSpeccy/USP, CLK, RustZX, JSSpeccy3 trap here (JSSpeccy uses PC==0x056B; USP/CLK 0x056B; Fuse checks PC==0x056C because PC is post-fetch-incremented off the RET NZ at 0x056B).
- 0x05ED = LD-SAMPLE edge sampler (the loop body most turbo loaders copy verbatim into RAM — signature anchor).
- 0x05E2 = RET at tail of LD-BYTES = the universal RESUME vector after a successful inject (Timex 0x0136). JSSpeccy sets PC=0x05E2 (byte there is 0xC9); CLK overwrites the fetched opcode with 0xC9; RustZX pops PC off the stack (lands on 0x053F). Fuse/ZEsarUX/JSpeccy force PC=0x05E2.
- 0x053F = SA/LD-RET, the return address PUSHed at entry (restores border, EI, returns to BASIC with carry).

128K / +2 / +2A / +3: same routine, gate on ROM1 (128/+2) or ROM3 (+2A/+3); Fuse uses the equivalent RET NZ at PC==0x0112 in the second ROM; Timex TC/TS2068 use EXROM (0x0112 load / 0x0136 return).

REGISTER/FLAG CONTRACT (read these BEFORE inject; note EX AF,AF' at 0x0557 means the live params are in the ALTERNATE set):
- A' = expected flag byte (0x00 header / 0xFF data)
- F' carry = LOAD(1) vs VERIFY(0)  — VERIFY must NOT be accelerated to a write; compare instead
- IX = destination address
- DE = requested byte count
ON EXIT (the authoritative Fuse trap_load_block spec, mirrored by JSpeccy/RustZX/USP/CLK):
- copy read=min(DE, len-1) bytes; if flag byte (data[0]) != A' → clear carry (error) and return
- A = running XOR parity (0 on success), B = 0xB0 success / 0x00 fail, C = 0x01, DE -= n, IX += n, H = parity, L = last byte, AF' = 0x0145
- carry SET on good checksum, CLEARED on flag/length/parity error
- reproduce the 48K ROM zero-length-block bug when DE==0
- resume PC = 0x05E2

MECHANISM: a fixed ROM PC trap on a single instruction inside LD-BYTES, gated by (a) ROM-page/identity check, (b) block type==ROM & state==PILOT & len==DE+2. Deterministic. No tempo, no edge routine, no per-loader knowledge for the standard case.
result.customLoaderStrategies:
How the best emulators reach instant/near-instant on TURBO/custom loaders — and which of these BulbuLator LACKS:

A) OPCODE-SIGNATURE DETECTOR + EDGE-LOOP SHORT-CIRCUIT (Fuse/ZEsarUX acceleration_detector + do_acceleration). They do NOT byte-inject custom loaders; they let the real loader run but recognize its edge-sampling loop by an opcode FSM over PC-6 and answer each IN instantly (poke B/C/carry, pop the loop RET). Covers Speedlock/Alkatraz/Bleepload/Microsphere/Paul-Owens/Digital-Integration/Search/Dinaload. LIMITATION for us: this technique deletes emulated HOST cycles — it only works because their CPU is software. It is NOT portable to a free-running fabric Z80. BulbuLator LACKS the signature TABLE (usable for classification) but cannot use the cycle-skip action verbatim.

B) FABRIC BUS-STUB INJECTION on a REAL Z80 (MiSTer smart_tape) — this IS portable and is our best hardware technique for turbo. Arm at M1 fetch 0x0562; drive the data bus with 0x00 (collapse pilot/sync) and a {JR $-2 ; LD L,n} handshake stub in the byte loop so the real ROM (or ROM-core-in-RAM) keeps running its own flag/parity/paging logic while each byte is fed instantly from a FIFO. BulbuLator LACKS this bus-injection stub path; it currently only byte-injects at block level and otherwise pulse/warps.

C) OFFLINE Z80-SIMULATION → SNAPSHOT (SkoolKit tap2sna --sim-load / loadtracer). Run the actual loader in a Z80 interpreter over the tape-as-edges, fast-forward its sampling loop with a ~43-entry accelerator table (each entry = loop byte-pattern + counter reg + ear_mask + loop_time + R-increment) plus generic DEC-A and contended-in handling, detect end-of-load, and inject the resulting RAM+register snapshot. ~99.95% coverage (3 failures / 6800+ files, all contended-timing loaders). BulbuLator LACKS this entirely — this is task #21 (SMART-2 ARM Z80 interpreter) and is the single biggest missing lever.

D) WHOLE-CORE WARP (ZEsarUX top_speed_timer, MiSTer 56MHz, Fuse fastload). Run everything unthrottled so the real loader finishes fast without any injection. BulbuLator HAS this (FAST/warp) but it is contention-capped ~4x on real silicon, so it is slow-but-correct, not instant, for tight turbo.

E) DIVMMC FIRMWARE SERVE — irrelevant for custom loaders (they bypass the ROM), and no audio path; gives up.

WHAT WE ARE MISSING, concretely: (1) a deterministic PC-trap decision replacing our tempo heuristic; (2) an opcode-signature classifier (the Fuse/SkoolKit tables) to positively identify a loader instead of guessing by read-rate; (3) MiSTer-style data-bus stub injection for ROM-core-in-RAM turbo loaders; (4) an ARM Z80 interpreter (tap2sna-class) with a loader-accelerator table to produce a snapshot for arbitrary/protected loaders.
result.tzxBlockMatrix:
Per TZX block ID — instant-injectable or pulse-only, and how (consensus of libspectrum/Fuse, CLK, JSSpeccy3, MiSTer):

0x10 Standard Speed Data — INSTANT byte-inject. Maps to LIBSPECTRUM_TAPE_BLOCK_ROM (same as every TAP block). Only type Fuse/RustZX/CLK/JSSpeccy accept for the trap. Payload = flag + data + checksum; inject via the standard-trap contract.

0x11 Turbo Speed Data — INSTANT byte-inject IS possible; the block ALREADY stores the decoded bytes at offset +0x12. The 18-byte header (pilot len, sync1, sync2, bit0, bit1, pilot-pulse-count, used-bits-in-last-byte, pause, 3-byte length) is needed ONLY to synthesize pulses for replay, NEVER to obtain the bytes. Fuse/RustZX/CLK do NOT inject 0x11 (they pulse it), but JSSpeccy3 AND BulbuLator already byte-inject 0x11 when the loader is ROM-driven — we are ahead here. Guard with the flag/length checks; walk 0x2x flow blocks even while injecting.

0x14 Pure Data — bytes present (no pilot/sync). Byte-injectable if consumed by a ROM-style path (JSSpeccy/BulbuLator inject 0x14); else pulse via pure_data_edge.

0x12 Pure Tone — PULSE ONLY (tone_edge; N pulses of given length).
0x13 Pulse Sequence — PULSE ONLY (explicit per-pulse lengths).
0x15 Direct Recording — PULSE/SAMPLE ONLY, never injectable (raw sampled bitstream at T-states/sample). Same class as WAV/CSW.
0x18 CSW Recording — PULSE ONLY (RLE/Z-RLE square wave); some parsers stub it.
0x19 Generalised Data — symbol-table + bit-packed; decodable to bytes in principle but complex; in practice PULSE-replay only (Fuse/CLK/MAME).

Flow/control (must be WALKED and honored even in inject mode, because turbo and standard blocks interleave with loops/pauses): 0x20 Pause/Stop, 0x21/0x22 Group start/end, 0x23 Jump (signed rel), 0x24/0x25 Loop start/end, 0x26/0x27 Call/Return, 0x28 Select, 0x2A Stop-if-48K, 0x2B Set signal level.

Metadata (SKIP for loading): 0x30 Text, 0x31 Message, 0x32 Archive info, 0x33 Hardware type, 0x35 Custom, 0x5A Glue, 0xFF header.

TAP files: every block is implicitly a 0x10/ROM block → 100% instant-injectable. A working TAP is itself proof the title uses the standard ROM loader.

Rule to adopt: byte-inject IDs 0x10/0x11/0x14 (already do); pulse/warp 0x12/0x13/0x15/0x18/0x19; interpret 0x20-0x2B/0x30-0x5A as flow/meta.
result.ourGap:
ROOT CAUSE of BulbuLator's lower hit-rate vs ZEsarUX/esxdos: we use the WRONG SIGNAL to decide instant-vs-pulse. Our SMART loader classifies standard-vs-custom by a TEMPO/ferate heuristic (SMP_CNT port-0xFE read rate, >800/0.5s → custom → PULSE fallback). Every reference emulator proves this is backwards: the instant decision is DETERMINISTIC — a PC trap at LD-BYTES (0x056B/0x0562) gated by the paged ROM bank and the block structure (type ROM, state PILOT, len==DE+2). Fuse and ZEsarUX use read-tempo (loader_detect_loader) ONLY for auto play/stop UX, never for load correctness. Because we gate instant on tempo, any standard loader whose leading behavior looks "fast/ambiguous" — animation, deliberate pauses, an unusual pilot, or the first fast reads before the ROM loop settles (exactly the BigThings/Critical Mass/Deflektor class) — gets false-classified as custom and dumped to PULSE, which is slow-but-correct. That is the observed "false-fallback" gap.

Every technique we LACK, precisely:
1. DETERMINISTIC standard trap as the decision maker: fire on fabric M1 fetch of 0x056B (48K) / 128K-ROM equivalents, gated by ROM-page identity (trap_check_rom: 48K ROM / 128 ROM1 / +3 ROM3 / Pentagon ROM1&!beta, and NOT DivMMC/ESXDOS/disk-IF) and by block-structure (type ROM/turbo, PILOT, len==DE+2). We react to tempo instead. This alone converts the false-fallback cases to instant.
2. Exact register/flag CONTRACT lock-down: A'/F'/IX/DE in, A=parity/B=0xB0/C=1/H=parity/L=last/AF'=0x0145/carry out, resume 0x05E2, plus the zero-length-block ROM bug and the VERIFY (F' carry clear) branch. We have SMART inject but must match this byte-for-byte to avoid the parity/EOT-class bugs already seen (Critical Mass).
3. OPCODE-SIGNATURE loader classifier (Fuse acceleration_detector table; SkoolKit's ~43-entry accelerator table): positively identify a loader / recognize the ROM-core-in-RAM (0x05ED clone) by its bytes near the trapped PC, instead of guessing by read-rate.
4. MiSTer-style DATA-BUS STUB injection for ROM-core-in-RAM turbo loaders on the real fabric Z80 (inject 0x00 over pilot/sync window + {JR $-2; LD L,n} handshake) — instant turbo without a full interpreter.
5. ARM Z80 INTERPRETER (task #21) running the loader offline over the edge model with the accelerator table → snapshot/PCAP inject: the only technique that instant-loads arbitrary protected/turbo loaders (tap2sna's >99% coverage). esxdos does NOT have this (it can't even pulse-fallback); ZEsarUX only whole-core-warps turbo. So this is where we can BEAT both.
6. We also don't currently reuse the DivMMC automap already in our fabric ($0562/$04C6/$1FF8 truth-table) as an alternate deterministic hook.
result.maxHitRateStrategy:
A five-tier deterministic ladder that matches esxdos on standard, matches/beats ZEsarUX on turbo, and beats both via an interpreter tier — with tempo demoted to a mere auto-start convenience:

TIER 0 (deterministic standard inject — replaces the tempo decision): Fabric raises an M1-fetch trap at PC==0x056B (48K) and the 128K/+2A/+3 ROM equivalents. Gate on (a) ROM-page identity (48K ROM / 128 ROM1 / +3 ROM3 / Pentagon ROM1 && !beta; suppress when ESXDOS/DivMMC/disk shadow paged) and (b) block structure (type ROM, state PILOT, len==DE+2). ARM freezes the T80, reads A'/F'/IX/DE, SMART-injects the block, writes the exact exit contract (A=parity, B=0xB0, C=1, H=parity, L=last, DE-=n, IX+=n, AF'=0x0145, carry, zero-length-bug, VERIFY branch), forces PC=0x05E2, resumes. Covers ~100% of TAP + TZX-0x10 with zero false-fallback. Immediately closes the observed gap.

TIER 1 (turbo byte-inject — keep/extend): directly inject TZX 0x11/0x14 payloads (bytes are stored decoded) whenever the loader drives the ROM path or is otherwise recognized; walk 0x20-0x2B flow blocks, skip metadata. We already do this and are ahead of Fuse here.

TIER 2 (real-Z80 turbo instant via bus stub + signature classify): port the Fuse/SkoolKit opcode-signature TABLE to the ARM to positively identify the loader (esp. the 0x05ED ROM-core-in-RAM clones — Speedlock/Bleepload/Alkatraz/etc.) from bytes near the trapped PC, then apply MiSTer-style data-bus stub injection (0x00 over pilot/sync, {JR $-2; LD L,n} byte handshake) so the real loader runs but each byte is fed instantly. Instant turbo for the dominant commercial families without a full interpreter.

TIER 3 (universal instant via ARM Z80 interpreter — task #21, the beat-everyone tier): for any loader not handled above, run it offline in the ARM Z80 interpreter over the tape-as-edges (tap2sna/loadtracer model) with the ~43-entry loader-accelerator table + generic DEC-A + contended-in, detect end-of-load (PC in RAM / ~3.5M T after tape end / timeout), and inject the resulting RAM+register snapshot into the fabric Z80 via the proven PCAP/state-load path. tap2sna hits >99.95% (3/6800+). This is the layer ZEsarUX and esxdos lack.

TIER 4 (universal correctness fallback — keep): pulse/edge replay + contention-safe warp for the residue interpretation can't reconstruct — contended-memory-timing-critical loaders, TZX 0x15 direct-recording, CSW/0x18, 0x19 generalised, and raw WAV/MP3. Always correct.

Tempo/ferate (SMP_CNT) is retained ONLY as an optional auto-PLAY convenience (Fuse loader_detect_loader thresholds: <=500T & B±1 x10 to start), never as the instant-vs-pulse decision. Net effect: instant for all standard + turbo-0x11/0x14 + all named turbo families + (via interpreter) essentially all protected loaders; pulse only for the genuinely un-decodable tail — a hit-rate at or above ZEsarUX+esxdos combined.

prioritizedPlan.technique: TIER 0: Deterministic fabric M1 PC-trap at 0x056B (+128K/+3 ROM equivalents) with ROM-page-identity gate + block-structure gate (type ROM, PILOT, len==DE+2); demote SMP_CNT tempo to auto-play only. Lock the exact register/flag exit contract (A=parity,B=0xB0,C=1,H=parity,L=last,DE-=n,IX+=n,AF'=0x0145,carry,zero-len bug,VERIFY branch), resume PC=0x05E2.
prioritizedPlan.gain: Eliminates the false-fallback; standard TAP + TZX-0x10 → ~100% instant with zero misclassification. Largest single hit-rate jump.
prioritizedPlan.where: FPGA fabric (M1 fetch trap + ROM-page/DivMMC-active signal to ARM) + ARM firmware (read regs, inject, force PC). Reuse existing SMART-inject + DivMMC $0562/$04C6/$1FF8 truth-table already in cores/zx-mister/rtl/divmmc.v.
prioritizedPlan.effort: Low-Medium. Trap + gate + contract already 80% present (SMART proven). Mostly rewiring the decision from tempo→PC and hardening the contract.

prioritizedPlan.technique: Keep/verify TIER 1 turbo byte-inject for TZX 0x11/0x14 (bytes stored decoded at +0x12); walk 0x20-0x2B flow blocks and skip metadata; apply the same flag/length guards.
prioritizedPlan.gain: Locks in the class we already beat Fuse on; prevents regressions on ROM-driven turbo/animated standard (BigThings-class).
prioritizedPlan.effort: Low. Already implemented per HANDOVER 2026-07-14; add flow-block walking + guard parity with Tier 0.

prioritizedPlan.technique: TIER 2: Port Fuse/SkoolKit opcode-signature loader classifier (ROM-core-in-RAM / 0x05ED clones: Speedlock, Alkatraz+variant, Bleepload, Microsphere, Paul Owens, Digital Integration, Search/Gremlin, Dinaload) as an ARM-side detector on port-0xFE reads; add MiSTer-style data-bus stub injection (0x00 over pilot/sync window; {JR $-2; LD L,n} byte handshake) so the real fabric Z80 keeps running while bytes are fed instantly.
prioritizedPlan.gain: Instant load for the dominant commercial turbo families without a full interpreter; converts the current EXOLON/Deflektor/Speedlock pulse-warp cases to instant.
prioritizedPlan.where: FPGA fabric (M1-snoop + data-bus drive/stub, arm@0x0562, disarm on leaving [0x53F,0x605)) + ARM firmware (signature table + byte FIFO producer).
prioritizedPlan.effort: Medium-High. Needs fabric data-bus injection (new) + porting the signature table; MiSTer smart_tape.sv is a near-drop-in RTL reference.

prioritizedPlan.technique: TIER 3: ARM Z80 interpreter (task #21 SMART-2) running the loader offline over the tape-as-edges with SkoolKit's ~43-entry loader-accelerator table + generic DEC-A + contended-in; end-of-load heuristics; inject resulting RAM+register snapshot into the fabric Z80 via PCAP/state-load.
prioritizedPlan.gain: Universal instant for arbitrary/protected/turbo loaders (~>99.95% per tap2sna). This is the tier that BEATS ZEsarUX (whole-core-warp only) and esxdos (standard-only, no audio path).
prioritizedPlan.where: ARM firmware (port SkoolKit loadtracer.py/simulator.py C build to bare-metal) + fabric (existing snapshot/PCAP state-load path).
prioritizedPlan.effort: High. New Z80 interpreter + accelerator table + end-of-load detection; but SkoolKit C simulator + t2sfiles are directly portable references and GPL-compatible.

prioritizedPlan.technique: TIER 4: Retain pulse/edge replay + contention-safe warp as universal correctness fallback for TZX 0x15/0x18/0x19, WAV/MP3, and contended-timing-critical loaders the interpreter can't reconstruct.
prioritizedPlan.gain: Guarantees no title ever fails; covers the residual long tail (correct, not instant).
prioritizedPlan.where: FPGA fabric (existing tape_player EAR edge path) + ARM (pulse generator).
prioritizedPlan.effort: None-Low. Already exists; just ensure it is the last resort, not the default.
